newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RGC says commodity prices hit profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RGC says commodity prices hit profit.

text.p: Miner RGC Ltd said on Thursday its lower operating profit for the six months to December 31 was due to lower commodity prices, non-gold divestments and the performance of the Porgera and Kundana gold mines.
RGC, which is 40 percent owned by Hanson Plc, reported an operating profit of A$25.9 million after tax and before an abnormal tax credit, down from A$33.7 million in the previous corresponding half.
The A$25.9 million figure takes account of an abnormal tax credit of A$7.36 million, recorded as a tax credit for prior year tax and timing differences.

In a statement accompanying its results, RGC said the result was affected by lower commodity prices, particularly for tin and copper, and the absence of majority-owned Pancontinental Ltd's non-gold operations.
These were sold in the second half of 1995/96.

The Porgera gold mine in Papua New Guinea contributed A$19.7 million, compared with A$23.7 million previously, while lower grades at the Kundana mine in Western Australia almost halved its profit contribution to A$5.3 million.
RGC said these adverse impacts were partly offset by higher prices for zircon and titanium dioxide products and the inclusion for the first time of Consolidated Rutile Ltd's results.
RGC last year acquired a majority stake in Cudgen RZ Ltd, which has a 50.1 percent stake in ConsRutile.
The group said it also benefited from improved operating performance at its Paddington gold mine in Western Australia, a lower net interest expense due to lower debt levels.
It earned a A$4.1 million profit on the sale of its interest in Discovery Petroleum NL, taken over last year by Premier Oil Plc.
